name: Government of Canada
description: The federal government of Canada, comprising the executive, legislative, and judicial branches. Headed by the Prime Minister. The federal public service includes roughly 130 departments and organizations with nearly 300,000 employees.

name: Parliament of Canada
description: The federal legislature of Canada, a bicameral body consisting of the Senate (upper house) and the House of Commons (lower house). The Parliament of Canada is located at Parliament Hill in Ottawa.

name: Senate of Canada
description: The upper house of the Parliament of Canada. Composed of 105 senators appointed by the Governor General on the advice of the Prime Minister. Senators serve until age 75.

name: House of Commons of Canada
description: The elected lower house of the Parliament of Canada. Consists of 343 members of Parliament (MPs) elected in single-member constituencies. As of 2025, the Liberal Party holds a minority government with 169 seats.

name: Supreme Court of Canada
description: The highest court of Canada, the final court of appeal in the Canadian judicial system. Comprises nine justices, including the Chief Justice of Canada. Has jurisdiction over all areas of law.

name: Department of Finance Canada
description: Central federal department responsible for economic and fiscal policy, tax policy, and financial sector policy. Currently led by Minister of Finance François-Philippe Champagne.

name: Global Affairs Canada
description: Federal department responsible for diplomatic and consular relations, international trade, and international development. Manages Canada's embassies and missions worldwide.

name: National Defence
description: Federal department responsible for the Canadian Armed Forces and defence policy. Currently led by Minister David McGuinty. The department includes the Canadian Coast Guard, Communications Security Establishment, and Defence Research and Development Canada.

name: Public Safety Canada
aliases: Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness Canada
description: Federal department responsible for public safety, emergency management, national security, and law enforcement. Oversees the RCMP, CBSA, CSIS, and Correctional Service Canada.

name: Canadian Space Agency
description: National space agency of Canada, established in 1989. Responsible for space science, exploration, and satellite communications. Known for the Canadarm and contributions to the ISS.

name: Statistics Canada
description: Canadian government agency responsible for producing statistics about Canada's population, resources, economy, society, and culture. One of the world's best statistical agencies.

name: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
aliases: Innovation, Sciences et Développement économique Canada
description: Federal department responsible for industry, science, and economic development. Oversees Statistics Canada, the Competition Bureau, the Canadian Space Agency, the National Research Council, and regional development agencies.

name: Health Canada
description: Federal department responsible for national health policy, drug regulation, and public health. Oversees the Public Health Agency of Canada and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency.

name: Canada Revenue Agency
description: Federal agency responsible for tax administration, tax collection, and the administration of tax laws and social and economic benefit programs. A separate agency with direct ministerial oversight.

name: Royal Canadian Mounted Police
description: Federal and national police service of Canada, providing law enforcement at the federal level and in many provinces and territories. Also responsible for national security, counter-terrorism, and protective services.

name: Bank of Canada
description: Canada's central bank, responsible for monetary policy, issuing currency, financial system stability, and funds management. Crown corporation established in 1934. Notable for its inflation-targeting framework.

name: Canada Post
description: Canada's primary postal service operator, a Crown corporation. Delivers to 16.5 million addresses across Canada. Processes approximately 6 billion pieces of mail annually.

name: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation
description: Canada's national public broadcaster, operating in both English (CBC) and French (Radio-Canada). Crown corporation established in 1936. Employs approximately 9,429 people. Revenue CA$515.84 million plus public funding.

name: VIA Rail Canada
description: Canadian Crown corporation operating intercity passenger rail service. Operates nearly 500 trains per week across 12,500 km of track, serving over 4 million passengers annually.

name: Export Development Canada
description: Crown corporation that provides financing and insurance to Canadian exporters. Facilitates over CA$100 billion in export trade annually.

name: Business Development Bank of Canada
description: Crown corporation providing financing, venture capital, and consulting services to Canadian small and medium-sized businesses. Administers over CA$40 billion in assets.

name: Atomic Energy of Canada Limited
description: Crown corporation responsible for nuclear energy research and development. Operates Chalk River Laboratories. Known for developing the CANDU reactor technology.

name: Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation
aliases: Société canadienne d'hypothèques et de logement
description: Crown corporation that provides mortgage loan insurance, housing policy research, and affordable housing programs. Key institution in Canada's housing market.

name: Royal Bank of Canada
description: Largest bank in Canada by assets (C$2,004.99 billion) and market capitalization (C$155.12 billion). Headquartered at Royal Bank Plaza, Toronto. Employs 91,398. One of the world's systemically important banks.

name: Toronto-Dominion Bank
description: Second-largest bank in Canada by assets (C$1,957 billion) and market cap (C$138.70 billion). Also the sixth-largest bank by branch network in North America. Employs 103,257.

name: Bank of Nova Scotia
description: Third-largest bank in Canada by assets (C$1,410.79 billion). Known for significant international operations in Latin America and the Caribbean. Employs 89,483.

name: Bank of Montreal
description: Fourth-largest bank in Canada by assets (C$1,293.20 billion). The oldest bank in Canada, founded in 1817. Headquartered at First Canadian Place, Toronto. Employs 55,767.

name: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce
description: Fifth-largest bank in Canada by assets (C$975.71 billion). Headquartered at CIBC Square, Toronto. Employs 48,074. Also operates Simplii Financial as a direct banking brand.

name: National Bank of Canada
description: Sixth-largest bank in Canada by assets (C$355.80 billion). The largest bank headquartered in Quebec. Sometimes included as the 'Big Six' with the Big Five. Employs 26,920.

name: Desjardins Group
description: Largest credit union federation in North America, with C$422.90 billion in assets. A federation of 313 autonomous credit unions (caisses populaires) primarily serving Quebec. Employs 56,165.

name: TMX Group
description: Operator of the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX), TSX Venture Exchange, and Montreal Exchange. Canada's primary exchange group for equities, derivatives, and fixed income.

name: Shopify
description: Canadian multinational e-commerce company. One of Canada's most valuable companies by market cap (~C$154 billion). Provides e-commerce platform for online stores and retail point-of-sale systems.

name: Enbridge
description: Canadian multinational energy infrastructure company. One of the largest pipeline companies in North America, operating the world's longest crude oil and liquid pipeline system. Market cap ~C$118 billion.

name: Canadian National Railway
description: Canadian Class I freight railway, the largest railway in Canada by revenue. Operates approximately 32,000 km of track spanning Canada and the United States, from the Atlantic to the Pacific.

name: Suncor Energy
description: Canadian integrated energy company, the largest energy company in Canada by revenue. Major developer of Alberta's oil sands. Also operates refineries and retail fuel stations (Petro-Canada).

name: Canadian Pacific Kansas City
description: Canadian Class I freight railway formed by the 2023 merger of Canadian Pacific Railway and Kansas City Southern. Operates the first single-line railway connecting Canada, the US, and Mexico.

name: Barrick Mining
description: Canadian mining company, one of the world's largest gold mining companies. Market cap ~C$104 billion. Operates mines across multiple continents.

name: Agnico Eagle Mines
description: Canadian gold mining company operating in Canada, Finland, and Mexico. One of the top gold producers globally. Market cap ~C$104 billion.

name: Brookfield Corporation
description: Canadian multinational alternative asset management company. One of the largest investors in real assets globally, managing over $900 billion in assets. Listed on TSX and NYSE.

name: Nutrien
description: Canadian fertilizer company, the world's largest potash producer and a major agricultural retailer. Formed by the 2018 merger of PotashCorp and Agrium.

name: TC Energy
description: Canadian energy infrastructure company operating natural gas pipelines, storage, and power generation across North America. Developer of the Coastal GasLink pipeline.

name: University of Toronto
description: Canada's top-ranked university and #1 research university (C$584,204 in sponsored research income). Ranked among the top 25 globally. Founded in 1827 as King's College.

name: University of British Columbia
description: One of Canada's top three research universities. Ranked among the top 40 globally. Major center for research in forestry, marine science, and biotechnology.

name: McGill University
description: One of Canada's most prestigious universities, ranked #3 in Canada for research income. Known for medical research and has produced 12 Nobel laureates. Founded in 1821.

name: University of Alberta
description: One of Canada's top 5 research universities. Ranked #1 in the Global Innovation Index 2025 for Canadian institutions (score 95.20). Known for AI research and energy studies.

name: Université de Montréal
description: Canada's #2 research university by total research income. A French-language university and one of the largest in Canada. Includes affiliated school HEC Montréal and Polytechnique Montréal.

name: McMaster University
description: Top Canadian medical doctoral university by research intensity (C$480,892). Known for its medical school and problem-based learning approach. Ranked #2 in Global Innovation Index for Canadian institutions.

name: University of Waterloo
description: Canada's leading technology and engineering university. Known for its co-op program and as a major AI research hub. Home to the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics.

name: University of Calgary
description: Major research university in Alberta, known for energy research, medicine, and engineering. Top 10 in Canada.

name: Dalhousie University
description: Atlantic Canada's leading research university. Known for ocean science, law, and medicine. Founded in 1818.

name: University of Ottawa
description: World's largest bilingual (English-French) university. Located in Canada's capital, known for law, social sciences, and health research.

name: Bell Media
description: Canada's largest broadcaster by revenue, a subsidiary of BCE Inc. Owns CTV Television Network, CTV News, and numerous radio stations and specialty channels. Over 30% of Canadian commercial television revenue.

name: Postmedia Network
description: Canada's largest newspaper chain. Owns the National Post, Toronto Sun, Montreal Gazette, Ottawa Citizen, and numerous other daily and community newspapers across Canada.

name: The Globe and Mail
description: One of Canada's two national newspapers. Known for its authoritative business and political reporting. Online readership of 11.4 million monthly.

name: Toronto Star
description: Canada's largest metropolitan daily newspaper by circulation. Known for investigative journalism with a progressive editorial stance. Online readership of 6.21 million monthly.

name: La Presse
description: Major French-language news outlet based in Montreal, now primarily digital. Online readership of 13.7 million monthly. One of the most influential French-language media in Canada.

name: Canadian Press
description: Canada's national news agency, providing news, photos, and data to media organizations across Canada. Founded in 1917.

name: CTV News
description: Canada's most-watched television news service, owned by Bell Media. Operates CTV National News, CTV News Channel, and local CTV stations across Canada.

name: National Post
description: One of Canada's two national newspapers, owned by Postmedia. Known for conservative-leaning editorial stance and business coverage.

name: Canadian Red Cross
description: Canadian national society of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. Provides disaster relief, health services, and humanitarian assistance.

name: World Vision Canada
description: Canadian branch of World Vision International, one of Canada's largest international development and humanitarian NGOs.

name: Plan International Canada
description: Canadian branch of Plan International, a major child rights and humanitarian organization.

name: United Way Centraide Canada
description: Canada's largest non-governmental funder of community social services. Operates through local chapters across Canada.

name: David Suzuki Foundation
description: Canadian environmental nonprofit organization founded by scientist David Suzuki. Focuses on climate change, biodiversity, and sustainability policy.

name: Liberal Party of Canada
description: Canada's governing party, currently led by Prime Minister Mark Carney. Centre to centre-left ideology (liberalism, social liberalism). Holds 174 of 343 seats in the House of Commons (as of 2026). Founded 1867.

name: Conservative Party of Canada
description: Canada's Official Opposition, led by Pierre Poilievre. Centre-right to right-wing ideology (conservatism, economic liberalism). Holds 140 of 343 seats. Founded 2003 (merger of Canadian Alliance and Progressive Conservative Party).

name: New Democratic Party
description: Canadian social democratic party, led by Avi Lewis. Centre-left to left-wing ideology (social democracy, democratic socialism). Holds 5 of 343 seats. Founded 1961, organizationally integrated with most provincial counterparts.

name: Bloc Québécois
description: Federal political party devoted to Quebec sovereignty and social democracy. Led by Yves-François Blanchet. Holds 22 of 343 seats. Centre-left ideology (Quebec sovereignty, regionalism). Runs candidates only in Quebec.

name: Green Party of Canada
description: Canadian environmentalist political party, co-led by Elizabeth May and Jonathan Pedneault. Holds 1 of 343 seats. Green politics ideology. Founded in 1983.

name: People's Party of Canada
description: Right-wing to far-right political party led by Maxime Bernier. Ideology: conservatism, right-libertarianism, right-wing populism. Founded 2018. No seats currently.

name: Canadian Armed Forces
description: The unified armed forces of Canada, comprising the Canadian Army, Royal Canadian Navy, and Royal Canadian Air Force. Led by Chief of Defence Staff General Jennie Carignan. Approximately 68,000 active personnel and 27,000 reserve.

name: Royal Canadian Navy
description: Naval force of the Canadian Armed Forces. Commands approximately 12 frigates, 4 submarines, and various coastal defense vessels. Led by Vice-Admiral Angus Topshee.

name: Canadian Army
description: Land force command of the Canadian Armed Forces. Led by Lieutenant-General Michael Wright. Regular force of approximately 22,500 and reserve of 18,000.

name: Royal Canadian Air Force
description: Aerial warfare force of the Canadian Armed Forces. Operates CF-18 Hornet fighters, CP-140 Aurora patrol aircraft, and various transport and search-and-rescue aircraft. Led by Lieutenant-General Jamie Speiser-Blanchet.

name: Canadian Special Operations Forces Command
aliases: Commandement des Forces d'opérations spéciales du Canada
description: Special operations command of the Canadian Armed Forces. Includes Joint Task Force 2 (JTF2), Canadian Special Operations Regiment (CSOR), and other specialized units.

name: Communications Security Establishment
aliases: Centre de la sécurité des télécommunications
description: Canada's signals intelligence and cybersecurity agency. Responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cybersecurity, and protecting government information. Part of the Department of National Defence.

name: Canadian Coast Guard
description: Canadian federal agency responsible for maritime search and rescue, navigation aids, icebreaking, and marine pollution response. A Special Operating Agency of the Department of National Defence since 2025.

name: International Development Research Centre
aliases: Centre de recherches pour le développement international
description: Canadian Crown corporation that supports research in developing countries. Part of Global Affairs Canada portfolio. Founded in 1970 by Parliament.
